content: MK asks whether the naw-mulḥidān label means freethinking subversives or neo-bāṭinīs, even Ismaʿilis, the last being possible given Timurid hostility to Ismaʿilis; he adds that Qāsim-i Anvār, Ṣāʾin al-Dīn's associate from his Cairo days, was apparently claimed by Ismaʿilis as one of their own and was to be exiled from Herat in 1427 along with Ṣāʾin al-Dīn for such suspect connections, though his putative Hurufi connection supplied the official excuse.
refers_to_primary: Shafique Virani, The Ismailis in the Middle Ages, 103-4 (via MK, fn 16)
